views.label: Resolve the catalog
views.note: The daemon resolves the project root and hands back the six roots plus confirmed page links.

views.label: Work inside daemon guardrails
views.note: The provider session reads pages on demand and reaches the repository only through Otto tools.

views.label: Deliver, then propose
views.note: The observable result returns first; durable knowledge is proposed at the end of the effort.

messages.label: send task
messages.note: The task is sent inside a workspace, which is what scopes everything downstream.

messages.label: WebSocket request
messages.note: Remote clients traverse the optional encrypted relay; daemon semantics stay the same.

messages.label: resolve root + catalog
messages.note: Worktree workspaces resolve to the repository project root, so branches do not fork project truth.

messages.label: six roots + confirmed links
messages.note: Confirmed pages only. Full page bodies are not returned here.

messages.label: start or resume
messages.note: The compact catalog is runtime-only for this session.

messages.label: read rich pages on demand
messages.note: Pull-on-demand: a page body is loaded only when the work needs it.

messages.label: invoke Otto tools
messages.note: Providers with native Otto tools consume the shared catalog directly; MCP-only providers receive it through the daemon adapter, without a second implementation.

messages.label: inspect or mutate
messages.note: Bounded by daemon guardrails. Preview starts the configured dev server and binds an Otto browser tab for verification.

messages.label: propose durable knowledge
messages.note: Written at the end of an effort, after the result is observable. Current truth changes only with a reason; evidence stays in an append-only timeline.

cards.title: The daemon owns the path
items: Reads and mutations run through the daemon, so every provider behaves the same way
The store location is decided in one place: project override, existing repository store, then host default
Worktrees resolve to one project store instead of forking project truth

cards.title: Catalog first, pages on demand
items: A session opens with the six roots and confirmed pages only
Full page bodies are read while the work runs, not preloaded
The catalog is runtime-only for the session that received it

cards.title: Neutral tools, late writes
items: Native and MCP-only providers share one tool catalog, not two implementations
Repository and service access stays inside daemon guardrails
Durable knowledge is proposed after the result, and current truth changes only with a reason
